key_insight: Exciton linewidths in polar semiconductors are not set by the Fröhlich constant alone; exact center-of-mass recoil plus electron-hole parity interference determines whether the 1s→1s phonon channel is open or suppressed.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar-cell and optoelectronic design, exciton mass symmetry and the dimensionless recoil parameters matter more than α alone when predicting resonance sharpness and thermal broadening.
method: Restored exact exciton center-of-mass recoil in the exciton-phonon scattering model.
Derived a parameter-free 1s→1s recoil channel at q* = sqrt(2M_ex ħω_LO)/ħ with rate proportional to N_LO(T).
Used hydrogenic Fröhlich-model parity/interference analysis to obtain suppression and linewidth scaling laws.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports calculated linewidths of 2.2 meV for GaAs, 0.00 meV for FAPbI3, and 0.12 meV for MAPbI3, and argues that observed 27–40 meV perovskite linewidths require additional inelastic channels beyond COM recoil.
watch_item: The conclusions are model-based and hydrogenic; real materials may need non-hydrogenic corrections, disorder, and additional phonon or defect scattering pathways.
paper_title: Why polar excitons stay sharp: parity protection of the center-of-mass recoil channel in exciton-phonon scattering
